what: Raymond James is a financial services firm built around its network of financial advisers, who manage money for individual clients. It also runs an investment bank, an asset manager, and a bank that lends to its own clients.
customers: Individual investors through advisers, corporate and municipal clients of the investment bank, and institutional asset management clients.
money: fees and commissions on client assets managed by advisers
investment banking, trading and municipal finance
lending to clients and interest on cash balances
moat: Advisers who own their client relationships and choose to affiliate with it rather than a bank-owned firm, which has made it a consistent recruiter of talent.
risks: Fee revenue falls when markets fall
Falling interest rates reduce income on client cash balances
Adviser recruitment costs rise when competition for them increases
opportunities: Revenue grew about 10% last year with a 15% net margin
Adviser headcount and client assets have grown consistently
Cash of about $10 billion against very little debt
watch: Net new assets and adviser recruitment, plus the yield on client cash.
